follow-up time: Throughout the duration of lactation (colostrum, transitional milk, mature milk)
exposure: Mode of delivery (vaginal vs. elective cesarean section)
cohort: The study included 21 women after vaginal delivery and 18 women after elective cesarean section, all healthy with normal newborns who were exclusively breastfed.
finding: While melatonin content in human milk decreased throughout lactation and showed consistent circadian rhythmicity regardless of delivery mode, daytime colostrum after cesarean section contained significantly higher melatonin levels compared to vaginal delivery.
mod_finding: Cesarean section was associated with higher melatonin levels in daytime colostrum compared to vaginal delivery.
